audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Sett all seven stages, which fits the 46.38% stored in the file for the early game but contradicts whys[4] ('the lane leverage flips decisively'), whys[5] ('making you the durable aggressor for the first time') and whys[6] ('your teamfight lockdown wins every objective fight'). The packet's chart reads Sett, Sett, Skill, Skill, Sejuani, Sejuani, Sejuani.
audit.why: The last three stages are described as Sejuani's in prose and as Sett's in the chart.
audit.corrected: Levels 3 and 4-5 should read Skill, and level 6, first item and two items should read Sejuani. Not written as edits — a side value cannot change inside the +/-10% length band. Raised in questionsForUser.

audit.why: Spikes at Sett 1-2, Sejuani 6, Sunfire and late are right, and Sunfire being the item that lets her hold the Q-W-E pattern through a Haymaker is the correct read.

audit.whatIsWrong: 1) Facebreaker is treated as an unconditional grab-stun in four places. Riot's text: it pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, and if enemies were only on one side they are slowed instead of stunned. In a 1v1 with nothing behind him it is a slow — and Fury of the North's Frost Armor grants immunity to slows, so it does nothing at all to a Sejuani who has been out of combat. That is the decisive interaction and it is absent. 2) Haymaker is described only as 'true damage'. It expends stored Grit for a shield as well, and the true damage is in the centre of the cone with physical damage on the sides — so where you stand changes the damage type. 3) Knuckle Down's two max-health-scaling attacks never appear, which is what actually makes his level 1 hurt a tank. 4) late calls his R a suppress; Riot's description says he carries a champion through the air and slams them.
audit.why: The player is told to fear a stun that usually is not one, and the two positional facts that decide the trade (which side of Facebreaker, which part of the Haymaker cone) are missing.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker's both-sides condition stated with Frost Armor's slow immunity, Haymaker described as Grit into shield plus a true-damage centre, Knuckle Down named, and the suppress wording dropped.

audit.whatIsWrong: No seconds anywhere despite the whole plan being 'fight when Facebreaker is down'.
audit.why: Facebreaker is 16s at rank 1 and Haymaker 18s — both long, which is why baiting them is a real plan rather than a hope.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to mid and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] says his trades 'drain your passive resistances'.
audit.why: The resistances are Fury of the North's Frost Armor, and what long trades actually do is keep it from rebuilding, since it only returns after time out of combat.
audit.corrected: Named and the out-of-combat condition used.

edits.after: Your Q-W-E combo is live and so is Facebreaker — but it only stuns with enemies on both sides of him, so keep his back clear and it is just a slow.

edits.after: Catch you with minions on his far side so Facebreaker stuns instead of slowing, then land the Haymaker into your face

edits.after: Stack Frost with W, then E-stun him — a one-sided Facebreaker only slows, and Frost Armor ignores it

edits.after: Charge his Grit bar with extended auto trades and keep you in combat so Frost Armor can never rebuild

edits.before: Level 3 gives you the full Q-W-E stun chain, and Sett gets Facebreaker — it is a genuine contest, so only commit the Q charge-in when his E is on cooldown and you can land the stun cleanly. From Level 4-5 you farm through the wave, track his Grit bar, and bait his Facebreaker with a short step-up so it is on cooldown for your real engage. Level 6 is your flip: Glacial Prison is a long-range projectile stun Sett has no dash to dodge, and every gank you receive now converts because the R stun into Jungler follow-up into E Permafrost is a guaranteed kill window on an immobile bruiser.
edits.after: Level 3 gives you the full Q-W-E stun chain, and Sett gets Facebreaker — a 16-second cooldown that only stuns when enemies stand on both sides of him, so keep his back clear and it is merely a slow Frost Armor shrugs off. From Level 4-5 you farm through the wave, track the Grit bar, and bait Facebreaker with a short step-up so it is down for your real engage. Level 6 is your flip: Glacial Prison is a long-range projectile stun Sett has no dash to dodge, and every gank converts because R into your jungler's follow-up into Permafrost is a guaranteed kill on an immobile bruiser.

edits.before: Level 1 belongs to Sett — his passive gives him a natural double-punch that trades efficiently before you have any Frost stacks built, so take W and last-hit at max range, letting him push. At Level 2 his Haymaker comes online and he will try to charge his Grit bar on you; respect that true damage and do not auto-trade into it. Your job through Level 2 is to track his W bar visually — a grey-bar Sett with no Grit is far less dangerous, and that is your window to step up and W-shred twice to apply Frost before retreating.
edits.after: Level 1 belongs to Sett — Pit Grit alternates his punches and Knuckle Down makes the next two hits scale off your max health, which is exactly the wrong thing to eat as a tank, so take W and last-hit at max range. At Level 2 his Haymaker comes online and he will try to charge his Grit bar on you; respect the true damage in the centre of that cone and do not auto-trade into it. Your job through Level 2 is to watch the grey bar — a Sett with no Grit is far less dangerous, and that is your window to step up, W-shred twice for Frost, and retreat so Frost Armor rebuilds.

edits.before: Once Sunfire Aegis is online you absorb his Haymaker true damage and trade positively through the full combo — your resistances outpace his sustained DPS, and every Q knock-up into double-W Frost into E stun resets the fight in your favor. In teamfights Sett has no answer to your R opening: you walk into range, throw Glacial Prison onto a carry, and by the time he R-suppresses one of your teammates you have already E-Permafrosted his front line. At two items you are essentially unkillable in a straight fight with him, and his team-fight value shrinks proportionally to your CC uptime.
edits.after: Once Sunfire Aegis is online you absorb his Haymaker and trade positively through the full combo — your resistances outpace his sustained DPS, and every Q knock-up into double-W Frost into E stun resets the fight in your favor. In teamfights Sett has no answer to your R opening: you walk into range, throw Glacial Prison onto a carry, and by the time he has carried one of your teammates into the ground with his R you have already Permafrosted his front line. At two items you are essentially unkillable in a straight fight with him, and his teamfight value shrinks as your CC uptime grows.

edits.before: - Sett Facebreaker: matchup-defining — The pull-stun starts his combo — stay off the line between him and units. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget Q dash for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Sett Facebreaker: 16s at rank 1, and it only stuns with enemies on both sides of him — keep his back clear and it is a slow Frost Armor ignores. - Haymaker: 18s, and the true damage is only in the centre. Step up on their downtime.

notes: The decisive interaction was missing entirely: Facebreaker stuns only when enemies are on opposite sides of Sett, and slows when they are all on one side — and Fury of the North's Frost Armor grants immunity to slows, so a clean 1v1 Facebreaker with nothing behind him does nothing to an out-of-combat Sejuani. The page had treated it as an unconditional grab-stun in four places. Haymaker was described as flat true damage; it expends stored Grit for a shield and only deals true damage in the centre of the cone, physical on the sides. Knuckle Down's max-health scaling was absent and is what makes his level 1 hurt a tank. Dropped the word 'suppress' for The Show Stopper — Riot's text says he carries a champion through the air and slams them, and I could not verify a suppression tag.
